paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Two groups in this passage are doing something with Jesus, and they could not be more different. In Caiaphas's courtyard, the chief priests and elders plot to arrest Him covertly and kill Him (Matthew 26:3-4). Meanwhile, in Bethany, a woman pours out her expensive perfume on Him, and Jesus calls it "a beautiful deed" (Matthew 26:10).

Now look at what Jesus says about her. The disciples see waste. Jesus sees something else: "By pouring this perfume on Me, she has prepared My body for burial" (Matthew 26:12). He had just told them He would be handed over to be crucified (Matthew 26:2), and she is the one who honors Him before it happens. Love for Jesus doesn't always look sensible to the people watching. Sometimes the best thing you give Him looks like too much, and He still calls it beautiful.

Then there's Judas, and I think this one hurts. He is one of the Twelve, and he walks to the very priests who were plotting and asks what they'll give him (Matthew 26:14-15). Being close to Jesus is one thing. Honoring Him is another. So here's my question for you, baker: when you come to Jesus, what are you pouring out, and what are you holding back? Keep your oven ready, because this story is just getting started.
